title: Positive scalar curvature forces rational inessentiality
main_claim: Every closed connected oriented n-manifold (n>=2) with a PSC metric is rationally inessential, i.e. (c_M)_*[M]=0 in H_n(BΓ;Q). There are no spin or dimension hypotheses. Corollaries: the Gromov–Lawson aspherical conjecture in all dimensions, flatness of nonnegative-scalar-curvature metrics on aspherical manifolds, the nonzero-degree-to-aspherical obstruction, and vanishing simplicial volume under nonnegative scalar curvature.

issues.location: Sec. 7, Thm 7.2 / citation of Cecchini–Schick Thm 1.14(1)
issues.description: The whole argument ends in an external result. It uses the local torical inequality of Cecchini–Schick, whose proof in dimensions above 8 depends on the Schoen–Yau 2017 minimal k-slicing theory. Here that theorem is applied in dimension q+kq, which is unbounded. The paper applies it correctly, but its correctness in all dimensions rests on that external GMT input.
issues.evidence: I fetched arXiv 1810.02116v4. Thm 1.14(1) reads: closed oriented X^n, f: X → S^1×T^{n-1} of nonzero degree, scal ≥ k0 and f ε-contracting on f^{-1}(J×T^{n-1}) imply 2πε ≥ √k0·Length(J). This matches the paper's quotation, and the constant is dimension-free. Remark 1.18 says the Schoen–Yau 2017 techniques are needed when dim > 8.

issues.location: Sec. 5, Thm 5.2 (uniform graph solvability on noncompact covers)
issues.description: The existence, uniqueness and parameter-smoothness argument for the quasilinear graph equation on the noncompact cover is only sketched. It goes by continuity method, limiting-chart maximum principles and a Jacobi-identity gradient bound. The steps I checked are sound, including the sign of the Jacobi identity, which I verified on a 1D curve example. Some routine details, such as compactness of limits and the Banach implicit-function setup, are left brief.
issues.evidence: Gradient estimate: at a minimum of v, εh_min/2 ≤ v(C_Ric + h_max·||dℓ||) because r^2 > 1/2. Barrier construction f_± = ε^{-1}(τℓ ± (π/2-δ)w) with λ ≥ B0·s^β > 0. Both are consistent.

sibling_notes: Rank 283 (the simplicial-volume companion) reported that its result depends on the companion's Cor 1.5 (nonnegative scalar curvature implies ||M||=0). This paper's Cor 1.7 proves exactly that, via Thm 1.1 plus the Ricci-flow/Milnor amenability reduction. I found no gap here, so that dependency appears sound, conditional on Schoen–Yau 2017 entering through Cecchini–Schick.
